Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Navy Federal Credit Unions denial of my fraud claim involving an unauthorized credit card transaction in the amount of {$1400.00}. On or about XX/XX/year>, I received notification that a charge for {$1400.00} had been placed on my Navy Federal XXXX Rewards credit card. I did not authorize, approve, or make this transaction. Upon receiving notification of the charge, I immediately contacted Navy Federal, reported the transaction as fraudulent, and filed a fraud claim. Navy Federal subsequently closed my card and issued a replacement card. The transaction was associated with a merchant identified as XXXX. I have never conducted business with this merchant. I do not use travel agencies and book all travel directly with airlines through their official applications or by contacting the airline directly. I received no travel itinerary, airline ticket, reservation, confirmation, or travel-related services associated with this transaction. After its investigation, Navy Federal denied my fraud claim, stating that no error had occurred. I requested additional information regarding the basis for the denial. Initially, Navy Federal responded that XXXX transaction data and its internal systems contradicted my claim of unauthorized activity but declined to provide specific details. After repeated requests for clarification, Navy Federal later informed me that its determination was based, at least in part, on records indicating that the transaction had been approved by text message from the phone number associated with my account. During a subsequent conversation with a Navy Federal representative, I was informed that an initial fraud alert had been declined and that a later alert had been approved. I reviewed my mobile phone billing records and confirmed that text activity occurred on the date in question from a five-digit short-code number. However, I do not recall receiving or responding to a fraud alert approving a {$1400.00} transaction with XXXX. The first notification I recall receiving was that a charge had already been placed on my account, at which point I immediately contacted Navy Federal and reported the transaction as unauthorized. Throughout this process, I have consistently maintained the following : I did not authorize, approve, or participate in this transaction. My credit card remained in my possession at all times. I have never conducted business with XXXX. I do not use travel agencies. I received no airline ticket, itinerary, reservation, confirmation, or travel-related services associated with this charge. I reported the transaction immediately upon becoming aware of it. Navy Federal closed and replaced my card following my fraud report. I also attempted to contact the merchant using the telephone number associated with the transaction but was unable to reach anyone. Additionally, I was unable to identify a verifiable business relationship between myself and the merchant. My concern is not that Navy Federal refuses to disclose proprietary fraud-detection methodologies. My concern is that despite multiple requests, Navy Federal has not provided meaningful responses to several critical factual questions that go directly to the basis of its determination. Specifically, I have requested clarification regarding : 1. Why was a second authorization request or fraud alert sent if the first fraud alert was reportedly declined? 2. What evidence exists that I received, used, or benefited from the travel services allegedly purchased through this transaction? 3. Did the merchant provide any passenger name records, airline ticket numbers, rental car/airlines reservation confirmations, itineraries, travel dates, email addresses, phone numbers, or other information connecting me to the services allegedly purchased? 4. What specific facts establish that I knowingly authorized this transaction beyond the assertion that a text response was received from the phone number associated with my account? Despite my requests, Navy Federal has repeatedly responded with generalized statements that its records contradict my claim while declining to address these specific questions. I respectfully request CFPB assistance in obtaining a substantive review of this matter and a clear explanation from Navy Federal regarding the factual basis for its determination that I authorized this transaction. I further request that Navy Federal address the specific questions outlined above and explain how it concluded that I knowingly authorized this charge despite my immediate fraud report, lack of any relationship with the merchant, and lack of receipt of any travel-related services. Thank you for your assistance and review of this complaint.

Despite my repeated efforts, the bank 's procedural errors, inconsistent guidance, and mishandling of my case have prevented a fair resolution and have caused me significant financial and personal hardship. From the beginning, I explained that this was a billing dispute involving unauthorized and disputed transactions. However, the claim was processed under the wrong category, and every subsequent action was affected by that initial error. I followed the bank 's instructions in good faith. Bank representatives instructed me to contact the merchant first before pursuing my dispute with the bank. I followed those instructions, which resulted in substantial delays. Later, I was repeatedly told that certain claims could not be reviewed because more than 60 days had passed. Those delays were not caused by me ; they were the direct result of the bank 's incorrect guidance and handling of my case. After the original Fraud Claim was closed, it was later reopened without my request and then used to classify valid Billing Disputes as duplicate claims instead of reviewing each disputed transaction individually. This prevented a proper investigation of my disputes. The attached documents also reveal serious inconsistencies in the bank 's investigation. For example, one denial letter states that Bank of America was unable to locate a disputed transaction for {$990.00}. Nevertheless, the bank denied the dispute. I respectfully question how a claim can be denied when the bank itself acknowledges that it could not locate the transaction being disputed. Another denial relied on the 60-day notification period even though the bank 's own procedural errors and incorrect claim classification substantially contributed to the delay. It is fundamentally unfair to penalize a customer for delays caused by the institution responsible for handling the dispute. Throughout this process, I received conflicting information from multiple representatives. During one conversation, a representative repeatedly insisted that I did not owe the bank money because my credit card limit was approximately {$1000.00}. However, this completely overlooked the central issue. This important distinction was never properly understood or investigated. Bank of America eventually returned part of the disputed funds and issued temporary credits, demonstrating that at least some errors were recognized. However, many disputed transactions remain unresolved, and I believe they deserve the same thorough and impartial review. This matter has caused me significant financial hardship, emotional distress, damage to my financial stability, and countless hours spent attempting to correct mistakes that were not of my making. I have contacted customer service, claims departments, management, and executive offices. Despite these efforts, I have not received a complete and fair resolution. I am submitting this complaint because I believe Bank of America 's procedural failures, incorrect claim classification, inconsistent handling, and inadequate investigation deprived me of a fair opportunity to recover my funds. XXXX ) prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce. Continuing to bill a consumer after explicit, repeated cancellation constitutes an unfair practice causing substantial, unavoidable injury. Restore Online Shoppers Confidence Act ( ROSCA ), XXXX XXXX. XXXX requires companies offering negative-option/recurring billing to provide simple cancellation mechanisms and honor them. Part 425 ) requires that cancellation be at least as easy as enrollment. Repeated failure to process cancellation across three channels demonstrates noncompliance. Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act UDAAP provisions ( 12 U.S.C. 5536 ( a ) ( 1 ) ) prohibits unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices by any covered person in connection with a consumer financial product or service. Electronic Fund Transfers/ Banking Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq. establishes consumer rights regarding electronic fund transfers, including the right to revoke authorization for preauthorized transfers. Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.10 ( b ) ( c ) specifically governs preauthorized electronic fund transfers from a consumers account. I provided cancellation notice the functional equivalent of a stop-payment instruction well in advance, through three independent channels, yet transfers continued. XXXX XXXX XXXXles ( if charges are processed via ACH debit rather than card rails ) require valid, current authorization for every debit entry and require that authorization be revoked upon consumer request. To the extent any of these transactions were processed as ACH debits, continued debiting after revocation also violates NACHAs authorization and revocation requirements. Between approximately XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, I became the victim of a highly sophisticated impersonation scam involving individuals posing as XXXX Support, Chase Bank 's Fraud Department, and federal officials. Through prolonged psychological coercion, they convinced both my elderly mother and me that we were participating in a confidential federal investigation and that we needed to move our money to protect it. During approximately XXXX month, Chase processed approximately XXXX extraordinary transactions totaling about {$790000.00}, including repeated cash withdrawals, cashier 's checks, and wire transfers used to purchase gold. Approximately {$100000.00} of these transactions involved my mother 's Chase account after she also became a victim of the same coordinated scam. These transactions occurred at numerous Chase branches and were completely inconsistent with our normal banking history. The transactions occurred repeatedly over approximately XXXX weeks and involved multiple branches, multiple transaction types, and unusually large dollar amounts. Viewed individually, each transaction may have appeared explainable. Viewed collectively, however, they reveal an escalating pattern of extraordinary activity. On multiple occasions, Chase employees questioned the transactions and warned me about scams. Because I believed I was already working with individuals I thought represented Chase 's Fraud Department and federal authorities, I responded exactly as I had been coached by the scammers. Despite repeated questions from branch employees and an escalating pattern of extraordinary transactions across multiple branches, the activity continued without what appeared to be centralized intervention, enhanced fraud review, or other protective measures. Because these transactions occurred across numerous Chase branches, I respectfully request that Chase determine whether its centralized fraud monitoring systems recognized the overall pattern of activity or whether each transaction was evaluated independently. Understanding how Chase 's systems evaluated this pattern is central to my complaint. My concern is not with the judgment of any individual branch employee. Rather, it is whether Chase 's overall fraud monitoring systems and procedures were sufficient to recognize and respond to an extraordinary pattern of high-risk transactions occurring across multiple branches over several weeks. I recognize that no fraud prevention system can stop every scam. However, when nearly {$800000.00} was withdrawn from XXXX customers ' Chase accounts through an unprecedented series of transactions within approximately XXXX month, I believe there should have been meaningful safeguards capable of recognizing that pattern and triggering higher-level intervention before catastrophic losses occurred. I am submitting this complaint not only because of my own losses but also because I believe my experience reveals a broader consumer protection issue involving sophisticated coercive scams that current banking safeguards may not adequately detect. My hope is that this review will result in a fair evaluation of my case while also helping identify opportunities to strengthen protections for future consumers facing sophisticated coercive scams.

This matter is at risk of escalating to a charge-off if not resolved promptly an outcome that would be directly and solely caused by Bank of America 's imposition of charges I dispute as improper. APPROXIMATELY TWO YEARS BEFORE THIS COMPLAINT : I opened a Bank of America credit card with a promotional financing offer and set up automatic payments for the minimum amount due. From the time I opened the account, I never received a single statement, notice, or communication of any kind from Bank of America not by mail, email, or any other means. Because automatic payments were handling the minimum due and I had received no correspondence whatsoever, I had no reason to believe anything was amiss. FIRST CONTACT FROM BANK OF AMERICA : The very first time Bank of America contacted me was a phone call placed several months after the promotional period had already ended, notifying me that a payment was overdue. I was so unaware of the account 's status that I initially told the representative I did not have a Bank of America credit card because I had never received a single statement or notice in the two years since opening the account. I had no knowledge the promotion had ended, no knowledge a balance remained, and no opportunity to act before the deadline passed. Upon being informed of the situation during that call, I immediately paid the full principal balance of approximately {$20000.00} in its entirety. I did not dispute the principal. I did not delay. I paid in full on the spot. Despite this, Bank of America is now demanding a substantial retroactive interest charge commonly known as " deferred interest '' backdated to the original date of purchase. This charge accrued silently over two years during which I received no statements, no promotional end-date notices, no warnings, and no communication of any kind from Bank of America . I believe this is deceptive and unjust for the following reasons : 1. Bank of America failed to send me any statements or notices for the entire life of the account approximately two years depriving me of any awareness of my account status or the approaching promotional deadline. 2. The first and only communication I received from Bank of America was a collections call placed months after the promotion had already expired far too late for me to act. 3. Upon receiving that first call, I immediately paid the full principal balance of approximately {$20000.00} in full, demonstrating my clear willingness and ability to resolve the account. 4. I didn't use the credit card during the relevant time and the only charge was an annual fee from XXXX XXXX that XXXX inadvertently charged to this card and couldn't reverse because Bank of America would not let XXXX reverse the charge - so I was forced to pay the XXXX charge to Bank of America, which I immediately paid after discovering the charge on a call with Bank of America while asking for the fees and interest to be waived. 5. When requesting a waiver of fees and interest, Bank of America stated that I could make a monthly payment under protest to avoid a charge off while I filed this complaint, so I made that monthly payment under protest. 6. The deferred interest charge now being demanded is entirely the result of Bank of America 's own failure to communicate not any negligence or bad faith on my part. 7. A charge-off, if it occurs, will result solely from Bank of America 's imposition of these disputed charges, not from any failure to pay a balance of which I was never properly notified. I am a customer who set up automatic payments, paid immediately upon being contacted, and paid {$20000.00} in full on the first call. The notion that I should now bear a large retroactive interest penalty accrued over two years of silence on Bank of America 's part and potential charge-off is fundamentally unfair. I am requesting that the CFPB investigate this matter urgently and direct Bank of America to waive the deferred interest charges in full. I am prepared to provide any documentation requested, including payment records and evidence of the absence of any statements or notices received. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint regarding a systemic flaw in credit reporting data pipeline mechanics that unfairly penalizes financially responsible consumers. Recently, Citibank/The Home Depot reduced my credit limit solely due to non-use. I do not owe a balance on this account.My complaint is not with the lender 's right to reduce the limit, but with the failure of the system to differentiate the reason for the reduction. Because banks do not transmit a specific 'inactivity ' reason code alongside limit drops, the automated credit scoring models automatically trigger a utilization penalty.The industry already has the trended data to fix this. The scoring models could easily review historical zero-balances to see that a drop was triggered by inactivity, not risk. Treating responsible, zero-balance behavior as an active risk metric creates a distorted reflection of consumer creditworthiness. I request that the CFPB push for data standardization requiring a distinct reporting classification for inactivity-based reductions versus risk-based reductions.

Consumer complaint narrative: I purchased goods with a debit card with an online retailer. The retailer placed a temporary hold of funds for items purchased. This did not reflect in my bank account amount. They released the temporary hold. My bank account still reflected no debit or pending charges even when I called to verify my current funds over the phone automated system. This gave me a false sense of reality with my funds in the bank because it showed an amount that was not truly there. When the items shipped, the items were then charged to my card. Thus, showcasing a " second '' charge. When a pending hold is placed and then released this finalizes a transaction, so to have this " charge the card '' when shipped makes a " second '' charge. This process can take as long as it takes for an item to ship so my bank account will not reflect the true amount until it is done. This process is very deceptive, misleading and confusing. This is a well-known situation within banks and card issuers and still persists. The real issue becomes when this causes negative funds due to this deception and false sense of reality. When the bank tells me what my account availability is they're responsible to tell the true honest reality. The retailer, card issuer and bank all need to be in communication with each other at point of sale. Some banks or cards will cause an overdraft fee which is deceptive due to faulty information given because they're not truly reflecting the point of sale because of this " hold and release ''. This situation is wrong and disingenuous. These banks and card issuers could be profiting off of what is well-known false information because of this type of online sale. This needs to be revised and addressed so that when a sale is made the amount is reflected accurately within the bank records to show what is truly available in real time. Returns are just as bad when being refunded to a card. When an item is returned the funding should be instant and not take days to process. Once the item is in the company 's possession a consumer 's funds should not be held up until its decided to be sent back. This should be immediate and a consumer should not have to wait for their own money. Some people need those funds immediately for other purchases elsewhere and need that money right there and have no reason to be without their money.

Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/XXXX, I discovered that my JPMorgan investment account had been used to process unauthorized debit card transactions. I immediately reported the fraud, canceled the debit card, and opened a fraud claim. After reviewing my account activity, I identified 314 debit card transactions between XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, totaling {$10000.00}. Only five transactions, totaling {$240.00}, were authorized by me. The remaining 309 transactions ( 98 % ) were unauthorized. The unauthorized activity began shortly after a legitimate debit card transaction I made in New York XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX, and continued for approximately nine months. The affected account is an investment account with a balance in the mid-six figures. Because investment balances naturally fluctuate with market performance, I primarily monitored the overall portfolio value rather than each individual debit card transaction. Changes of XXXXl XXXX XXXX over days or weeks are common in an investment portfolio of this size and could reasonably be attributed to normal market fluctuations. I was also unaware that my debit card was linked to this investment account. I had always used my checking account for my everyday purchases, and I rarely used this debit card. I understood that the investment account was intended primarily for investing, and I would access those funds only if I specifically needed to do so. Throughout the investigation, I repeatedly requested an explanation regarding how and why the debit card was linked to this investment account but did not receive a substantive response. The unauthorized activity followed clear and repetitive patterns involving a small number of merchants. One merchant alone accounted for 137 debit card charges totaling {$4100.00}, including as many as eight transactions in a single day, with recurring dollar amounts and purchase-and-return activity. Another merchant accounted for 50 debit card charges, including 14 transactions in a single day. Additional merchants accounted for 35, 19, and 12 debit card charges, respectively, each exhibiting repeated transaction patterns over short periods. A summary of these transaction patterns is attached. Shortly after I reported the fraud, JPMorgan reimbursed {$850.00}, representing only the most recent unauthorized transactions that the bank determined were eligible for reimbursement. The remaining unauthorized transactions continued under investigation for several months. During that time, I fully cooperated with every request made by the bank, including reviewing each transaction and identifying which transactions were authorized and unauthorized. I also repeatedly requested an explanation regarding the banks fraud investigation, the absence of fraud alerts or intervention, the linkage of my debit card to my investment account, and the basis for the reimbursement decision. After approximately five months of investigation, JPMorgan ultimately denied reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized transactions, stating that I was responsible for reviewing my account statements. I respectfully disagree with that determination. While I understand the importance of monitoring my accounts, I also believe banks have an important role in monitoring and investigating unusual account activity. In this case, the bank determined that a portion of the unauthorized transactions warranted reimbursement, yet denied reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized transactions arising from the same prolonged pattern of activity. Despite months of investigation, I have not received a satisfactory explanation regarding the repetitive transaction patterns, the absence of fraud alerts or intervention, the linkage of my debit card to my investment account, or the basis for denying reimbursement for the earlier unauthorized transactions. I respectfully request that the CFPB review JPMorgans handling of my fraud claim and assist in obtaining reimbursement for the remaining unauthorized debit card transactions. I also request that the bank provide a complete explanation of its fraud investigation, fraud monitoring, and claim determination.

In this case : - The merchandise received was not authentic as advertised ( counterfeit goods ). - The goods materially differed from the description and branding presented at the time of sale. - The merchant failed to respond or comply with its stated return/refund process. - I submitted timely and repeated dispute notifications with supporting documentation. -- - # # # Failure of Investigation and Improper Dispute Handling Goldman Sachs has failed to conduct a meaningful review of the evidence provided. Each denial incorrectly reduces the issue to authorized purchase, without addressing whether the goods were counterfeit or materially different from what was advertised. This reflects a failure to properly investigate under FCBA and Regulation Z requirements, which obligate card issuers to investigate billing disputes in good faith and consider all submitted documentation. Despite multiple submissions, including : - Photographic and descriptive evidence of counterfeit indicators - Merchant policy violations - Proof of non-response from the merchant - Evidence of widespread consumer complaints regarding identical fraud patterns No substantive analysis of the counterfeit claim has been provided. -- - # # # Additional Consumer Harm & Pattern Evidence The merchant in question has been widely reported by other consumers for : - Selling counterfeit or diluted luxury goods- Using inconsistent or non-verifiable shipping addresses- Failing to honor refund and return policies- Non-response to customer service inquiries These factors further support that this is not an isolated dissatisfaction issue, but a pattern of deceptive commercial conduct. -- - # # # Requested Resolution I am requesting that the CFPB require Goldman Sachs Bank USA to : 1. Reverse the charge in the amount of {$150.00} 4. Confirm in writing the specific basis for any final determination, including direct response to counterfeit and misrepresentation claims 5. Review internal dispute handling procedures to ensure compliance with FCBA requirements for good-faith investigation I have made repeated good-faith attempts to resolve this issue directly through the card issuer process, providing extensive supporting documentation each time. The continued failure to address the counterfeit nature of the goods or to meaningfully engage with the evidence submitted demonstrates a breakdown in the required dispute resolution process under federal consumer protection law. The company in question is no longer in business due to their fraudulent practices. I have filed cases with the XXXX and the Federal Trade Commission. I respectfully request CFPB intervention to ensure proper handling of this dispute in accordance with the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: A significant part of my complaint concerns not only the merchant 's conduct, but also Apple Card 's handling of the dispute process itself. The reason I am unable to provide traditional supporting documentation is because the merchant failed to provide it at every stage of the transaction. I never received an order confirmation email, receipt, order number, or any other proof of purchase after being charged. When I returned the item in-store, I specifically requested documentation confirming the return. Store employees informed me that they could not provide a receipt because their printer was broken. Later, when I contacted customer service regarding the missing refund, I was told that the merchant had no record of the transaction at all. In other words, the entire premise of this dispute is that the merchant failed to generate, maintain, or provide basic transaction records. The absence of documentation is not evidence against my claim ; it is the very reason the claim exists. Despite this, Apple Card repeatedly treated the lack of documentation as though it were my responsibility rather than the merchant 's. Over the course of more than two months, I made repeated phone calls, submitted written explanations, responded to requests for information, and attempted to provide every piece of evidence available to me. I also made good-faith efforts to resolve the matter directly with the merchant before involving Apple Card XXXX Each time I contacted Apple Card, I was forced to re-explain the facts from the beginning. On multiple occasions, I was informed that the dispute had been closed or decided despite the fact that the merchant still had not produced basic proof supporting its position. I repeatedly requested that the matter be reviewed and reopened because fundamental questions remained unanswered. Why was the merchant unable to produce a receipt, order confirmation, or transaction record? Why was the merchant permitted to claim I agreed to terms and conditions when it could not even establish the existence of the underlying transaction? Why was the merchant allowed to retain both the returned merchandise and the funds without providing proof that it had fulfilled its obligations? To this day, neither Apple Card nor the merchant has provided me with documentary evidence showing that the merchant has a valid basis for retaining my funds. Instead, Apple Card appears to have accepted the merchant 's position at face value while holding me to an impossible standard : producing documents that the merchant itself failed to provide and now claims do not exist. What I find most troubling is that Apple Card repeatedly relied on the assertion that I agreed to the merchant 's terms and conditions, while simultaneously failing to provide any evidence that such an agreement occurred. If the merchant can not locate the transaction, can not produce a receipt, can not produce an order confirmation, and can not provide a record of the purchase, then it is unclear how Apple Card determined that there was sufficient evidence to deny the dispute. I have been a loyal Apple Card customer for years and have trusted that disputed transactions would be investigated fairly and impartially. Instead, I have spent months repeatedly calling, emailing, reopening disputes, and providing detailed explanations, only to receive conclusions that appear unsupported by the evidence available. Throughout this process, I have cooperated fully, responded promptly, and made every reasonable effort to resolve the issue. The merchant, by contrast, has been unable to produce basic records of either the purchase or the return. The result is that I am being held financially responsible for a transaction that the merchant can not properly document, for merchandise that I no longer possess because it was returned to the merchant, and for a refund that was promised but never issued. I believe Apple Card failed to conduct a reasonable investigation, failed to require adequate substantiation from the merchant, and unfairly placed the burden of the merchant 's recordkeeping failures on me.

On or about XXXX XXXX XXXX, Citibank closed all of my accounts : two checking accounts and a XXXX XXXX account at the bank, along with my associated Citi XXXX XXXX XXXX rollover IRA. Citibank cited an incomplete " Know Your Customer '' ( KYC ) review ( Citi KYC Reference ID XXXX ). The closure cut off my access to my funds and ended a 29-year banking relationship. I am pursuing the brokerage rollover IRA, and the risk that its forced closure triggers tax and early-withdrawal consequences, separately with the appropriate securities regulator ; I note it here only to show the full scope of the closure. The closure was not the result of any failure to cooperate on my part. The KYC review opened around XX/XX/XXXX. Because my assigned financial advisor ( XXXX XXXX ) failed to advance the process, I personally called Citi 's KYC department on at least three occasions ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX ) and provided every item requested. Citi recorded each of these calls. On these calls I : - Corrected inaccurate information in Citi 's own KYC profile, including a long-dissolved former employer ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX which ceased operations in XXXX ) and a phantom company ( " XXXX XXXX '' ) that Citi had listed as my source of wealth. The correct entity is XXXX XXXX XXXX, my own registered LLC. - Provided detailed source-of-wealth information and, at Citi 's request, supplied statements from external retirement and brokerage accounts to substantiate that my Citi holdings were consistent with my stated net worth. - Was told by Citi 's KYC representatives that the review was essentially complete and that no further action was required from me. Despite this, Citi issued a closure-warning letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ( closure date XX/XX/XXXX ) and ultimately closed all of my accounts. On XX/XX/XXXX, my Citi Wealth Relationship XXXX emailed me acknowledging that I had been " incredibly cooperative and transparent, '' stating that the closure was unexpected, and confirming that she had escalated the matter to KYC management to seek reopening. On XX/XX/XXXX, two members of Citi 's Florida wealth-management leadership called me directly and acknowledged, on a recorded Citi line , that the closure of my accounts was caused by a defect in Citi 's own systems and not by any failure on my part. They confirmed I had cooperated and provided the requested information " each and every time, '' and stated that my accounts were closed even though I had done so. They described this as a recurring " glitch '' in Citi 's systems that they are actively working to repair, stated that it is affecting " far too many '' Citi customers across multiple business lines including Citi Private Bank, and said they had escalated the problem that day to senior Citi operations leadership. They called the treatment of a 29-year relationship " inexcusable, '' and offered to attempt to re-establish my accounts and reverse the resulting charges. XXXX XXXX also committed to send me a written follow-up. This was a management-level admission that my accounts were wrongfully closed by a known, systemic process failure, not for any legitimate compliance reason. Citi has only partly honored those commitments, and its internal handling remains contradictory. As of the date of this complaint, Citibank has reopened my primary 29-year joint checking account ( ending XXXX ), which I can again use. That reopening, however, was incomplete and left the account functionally impaired by the same systems Citi 's management has admitted are defective : my ATM/debit cards were never reinstated and remained blocked even after the accounts were reopened a defect Citibank discovered only when I happened to flag it on XX/XX/XXXX and my household was silently dropped from the account 's subscription-rebate ( perks ) benefit program when Citi 's system closed and reopened the accounts. Both had to be corrected manually after the fact. The second checking account ( ending XXXX ) remains closed ; it existed only to link my departing IRA, so I do not seek its restoration. The XXXX XXXX account ( ending XXXX ) is open but unfunded. XXXX XXXX never sent the written follow-up or the direct contact information he committed to provide on XX/XX/XXXX, now more than a week ago. On XX/XX/XXXX, two Citi units gave me directly contradictory information on the same day. My wealth relationship manager 's office emailed asking me to re-document my " source of wealth '' on a business questionnaire, while Citi 's KYC department confirmed to me on a recorded call that my source of wealth had already been accepted in XXXX and that the review was " satisfied/approved '' on XX/XX/XXXX with " nothing else needed. '' Closure-related charges have continued, and the disruption from the wrongful closure of a XXXX relationship remains ongoing and unremedied. That same evening ( XX/XX/XXXX ), Citibank restricted every one of my accounts again under a new case reference ( XXXX ), hours after its own KYC department had confirmed on a recorded line that the prior review was satisfied and there was no block. The restriction bars deposits, transfers, and withdrawals from my bank accounts and warns that if I do not act, Citibank will liquidate my retirement account and mail me a check. The restriction notice states that my accounts were restricted because I " have not yet provided critical, missing information, '' frames the restriction as something I can " easily lift '' by providing that information, and presents closure as avoidable by a XX/XX/XXXX deadline. It presents the restriction, in other words, as a conditional and preventable consequence within my control. That stated basis is false on Citi 's own record. Citi 's KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day that I had already provided the information, that it was accepted in XXXX, and that there was " no block. '' And on XX/XX/XXXX, my own Citi relationship manager confirmed to me in writing that the restriction is procedural, that the case is simply being finalized internally, and that there is " no new needed information '' from me. Citibank nonetheless imposed the full restriction immediately, on a stated basis its own employees had already disproved. The adverse action was taken first. It was not a future consequence I could avert by supplying anything, because Citi confirms there is nothing left for me to supply. Citibank subsequently lifted the restriction on my deposit accounts my joint checking was usable again within days yet it has continued to generate and mail me the same restriction notices. A mailed copy of the XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice reached me about a week later, on or about XX/XX/XXXX. When I called Citibank about it, a representative told me that no further information was needed, that the case was simply being finalized, and that Citibank 's system " will periodically continue to send notices until the case is closed, '' so I should " disregard '' the notice. Citibank is thus mailing a 29-year customer formal notices that state he failed to provide " critical, missing information '' and threaten to liquidate his retirement account, while simultaneously instructing him to ignore those notices because nothing is in fact outstanding. A consumer can not reliably tell a genuine restriction notice from XXXX Citibank will later say to disregard. This was still unresolved as of XX/XX/XXXX. Roughly two weeks after Citibank 's representatives first told me the review was in its " final stages, '' I called Citibank 's KYC department again to confirm my status. A representative told me my accounts were unblocked, but that the review remained open and was in a " disposition '' stage that had been handed to another Citibank department for a final approval she could neither see nor expedite, with no further information needed from me. She again offered to request a written " KYC satisfied '' letter once the review closes a letter I have asked for repeatedly and still do not have. To date, Citibank has never rescinded its XX/XX/XXXX restriction notice in writing. That notice still states on its face that my Citi accounts will be closed, and my retirement account liquidated and mailed to me as a check, if I do not provide information by XX/XX/XXXX the very notice Citibank 's representatives have told me to disregard because nothing is in fact outstanding. More than two weeks after Citibank 's personnel began telling me the matter was in its " final stages, '' Citibank still has not given me a single authoritative written answer reconciling that standing closure-and-liquidation notice with its assurances that I owe it nothing further. Underlying every step of this is a single, systemic failure : Citibank 's automated KYC and account-closure processes took adverse action against a fully compliant 29-year customer, repeated it, and would not release it and no person at Citibank has been able to stop or override it. My assigned financial advisor wrote to me that the closure was " beyond our control. '' My relationship manager advocated for me for weeks, including on weekends and after hours, yet the restriction persisted and the false notices kept arriving. Citibank 's own Florida wealth-management leadership admitted the closure was a system defect, said they had escalated it to senior bank-operations leadership, and still could neither prevent the renewed restriction nor stop Citibank 's systems from mailing me notices they themselves told me to disregard to the point that, in XXXX XXXX, a senior Citibank manager was reduced to escalating internally to try to switch off the bank 's automated " missing information '' messages, which the system continued to generate by default. When a bank 's own advisor, relationship manager, and senior management all acknowledge the customer did nothing wrong and still can not stop the bank 's systems from closing his accounts, freezing his retirement assets, and mailing him false liquidation threats, the failure is systemic not the error of any one employee. I am asking the CFPB to require Citibank to : ( 1 ) produce the recordings of my XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX KYC calls under Reference ID XXXX, and the XX/XX/XXXX call from its wealth-management leadership ; ( 2 ) explain the basis for closing and then restricting my accounts after its own representatives confirmed my compliance and after its own management attributed the closure to a system defect, including how it could restrict my accounts for " missing information '' that its own KYC department confirmed on a recorded call the same day, and that its own relationship manager confirmed in writing on XX/XX/XXXX, had already been provided and accepted ; ( 3 ) reverse any fees or third-party charges ( e.g., stop-payment fees ) caused by the closure ; ( 4 ) correct the inaccurate source-of-wealth/employment records that drove the adverse action ; and ( 5 ) given Citi management 's own statement that this defect is affecting " far too many '' customers, examine whether other consumers have been subjected to the same wrongful closures.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am writing to formally document a series of service failures that I believe warrant immediate review and remediation. As an XXXX military service member with an established record of consistent, on-time payment history, I have long maintained a relationship of good standing with American Express. It is with considerable disappointment that I submit this complaint. In the weeks preceding this correspondence, my military compensation was subjected to an institutional delay coinciding with the XXXX XXXX period a circumstance wholly beyond my control. This financial disruption was compounded by the sudden and unexpected passing of my father. Recognizing the potential risk of returned payments, and in a proactive effort to safeguard my account standing, I initiated several additional manual payments by telephone in anticipation of my payroll deposit arriving imminently. Regrettably, that deposit did not materialize within the expected timeframe. It is my understanding that the subsequent account cancellation was not the result of a human review or deliberate determination, but rather was triggered algorithmically an automated response that failed to account for the totality of my circumstances, including the manual payments I had submitted in good faith, my consistent payment history, and the documented military pay delay I had proactively communicated to your representatives. Throughout this period, I maintained open communication with American Express representatives, clearly articulating the nature of the delay and receiving assurances that all relevant notations were being recorded in my account file. Upon returning from my father 's funeral services, I contacted American Express on XX/XX/XXXX via both telephone and in-app chat to provide a comprehensive account of the circumstances. Despite these documented communications and the extenuating nature of my situation, the company 's systems had already proceeded to cancel my accounts. When I subsequently requested to be transferred to American Express 's dedicated Military Services line citing my XXXX status and my eligibility under the Service-members Civil Relief Act the representative declined to facilitate this transfer on the basis that my accounts had already been cancelled. I was informed that my only recourse was enrollment in a repayment arrangement. This response, delivered without acknowledgment of my bereavement or my protected military status, was experienced as procedurally rigid and devoid of basic compassion. The sole resolution offered was a 48-month Financial Relief Program at an interest rate of 5.89 %, with no assurance of account reinstatement upon completion. When I offered to provide a death certificate as supporting documentation, the representative responded in a manner that appeared scripted and dismissive, making no effort to consider the full context of my circumstances before redirecting me toward a program I had not been afforded adequate time to evaluate. The telephone call subsequently disconnected, and my attempt to continue via the in-app chat platform was similarly interrupted due to connectivity limitations at my remote location. The in-app representative likewise exhibited a scripted, formulaic tone that reflected no individualized consideration of my case. I wish to be unequivocal in stating that I am committed to fulfilling my financial obligations. However, I firmly contend that the cancellation of my accounts precipitated by an involuntary military pay delay during a period of personal bereavement, and triggered by an automated system rather than an informed human determination constitutes a disproportionate and inequitable outcome. My account history stands as a testament to my reliability and loyalty as a customer, and I respectfully object to being subjected to a hard credit inquiry or a comprehensive credit re-evaluation in order to restore access to accounts I have maintained in good standing. I am requesting that American Express conduct a thorough review of this matter and take corrective action consistent with both my documented account history and the protections afforded to active-duty service members under applicable federal law. Specifically, I am seeking reinstatement of my account privileges without the imposition of a new credit evaluation process. I appreciate the longstanding relationship I have maintained with American Express and remain hopeful that this matter will be resolved equitably and with the consideration it deserves. I await your formal response and determination. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX : XXXX

American Express had before it all of the information I was able to provide, including documentation and evidence supporting my position. However, despite acknowledging that it had not identified any independent verification of the agreement or its execution data, it nevertheless chose to rely on that agreement to uphold the charges. He stated that an unauthorized individual had obtained my account number and routing number and that I would need to establish a new account. He advised me that funds had been moved in three transactions : {$5000.00}, {$5000.00}, and {$5900.00}. The caller instructed me to log into my online banking account. My checking account showed a balance of {$15000.00}, which did not equal the total amount that had previously existed across our five accounts. Based on the balances that existed before the incident, approximately {$18000.00} should have been present across those accounts. This means that approximately {$2800.00} was unaccounted for at the time I reviewed the balances. This discrepancy further increased my concern that unauthorized transactions had occurred and that funds were missing from our accounts. At this point I was in a state of panic and believed I was working directly with an RBFCU fraud representative. The caller instructed me to verify my username and then directed me to process transfers involving the amounts he had identified. He represented these actions as necessary steps to move funds into a new secure account. He then scheduled another appointment for XX/XX/year>, to establish new account information. No one from RBFCU contacted me on XX/XX/XXXX as promised. I attempted to call the credit union but was unable to remain on hold because of work obligations. She asked whether I had provided my username and indicated that customers should never provide that information. However, during the same conversation she immediately requested my username to verify my account, which I found confusing and inconsistent. I was then transferred to the fraud department where a fraud claim was opened. The representative informed me that one transaction had already been flagged as suspicious and that I might be able to recover those funds. However, she did not obtain a complete statement regarding the events that occurred, did not ask for a detailed timeline, did not provide meaningful guidance regarding securing my accounts, did not offer assistance opening replacement accounts, and did not explain how I could regain access to my online banking. After reviewing my account, XXXX initially stated, " Ma'am, there is no fraud claim on this account. '' I then provided him with the fraud claim number I had been given. Only after I supplied the case number did he acknowledge that a claim existed and state that he could see it in the system. During that conversation XXXX asked me to answer my account security question. He informed me that my answer was incorrect. He then changed my security question to a new one. This raised serious concerns because the answer I provided had previously been correct. The fact that my security question had apparently been altered suggests that unauthorized changes may have been made to my account security settings. At no point during the conversation did XXXX address how or when the security question had been changed, who had changed it, or whether this indicated additional unauthorized access to my account. I also asked XXXX whether my daughter needed to open a separate fraud claim because her accounts had also been affected. XXXX specifically advised that she did not need to file her own claim because our accounts were linked. However, when my daughter later visited RBFCU on two separate occasions, two different employees informed her that she should have opened her own fraud claim. This conflicting information created confusion and raises concerns regarding whether her losses were properly documented and investigated. During the same call, XXXX instructed me to open a new checking account and a new savings account, which I did. I explained that the caller possessed sensitive account information before I ever disclosed my username and appeared to have access to information that should not have been available to an unauthorized individual. I am concerned that unauthorized access to my account occurred before I disclosed any information and I request that the credit union investigate whether an account compromise, security failure, or other unauthorized access event occurred. Throughout this process I have received conflicting information from multiple RBFCU employees regarding the existence of my fraud claim, account security changes, whether my daughter required her own claim, and how reimbursement funds would be handled. These inconsistencies have made it extremely difficult to understand the status of the investigation and have undermined my confidence in the credit union 's handling of this matter. My concerns include the following : 1. RBFCU did not obtain a complete statement regarding the fraudulent activity before beginning its investigation. 2. RBFCU employees provided inconsistent and contradictory information regarding account security, fraud reporting requirements, and investigation procedures. 3. I was not provided timely or adequate assistance in securing my accounts or regaining access to my banking services. 4. My daughter and I were left without reliable access to our accounts and banking services. 5. Apparently unauthorized changes were made to my account security settings, including my security question, and these changes were not adequately investigated or explained. 6. I am concerned that RBFCU may be improperly treating these transactions as authorized solely because I was deceived by an individual impersonating a bank employee. 7. I request confirmation that RBFCU is conducting a full Regulation E investigation into all unauthorized electronic fund transfers associated with this incident. 8. I request that RBFCU provide any provisional credit required under Regulation E while the investigation remains pending. 9. I request a full accounting of all transactions, account changes, security setting modifications, login activity, and investigative findings related to this incident. I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau review RBFCU 's handling of this matter, ensure that a thorough investigation is conducted, and require the credit union to provide a clear explanation of its findings and compliance with applicable consumer protection laws and Regulation E requirements. Thank you for your assistance. XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: PORTAL NARRATIVE U.S. Bank Official Check # XXXX U.S. Bank 's fraud and risk reporting infrastructure contains a structural blind spot : named payees on active official checks have no recognized standing to report risk to the issuing bank. The third-party remitter controls all remedies. The payee, whose name and address are physically printed on the instrument, is invisible to the bank 's intake system. This complaint documents what happens when that gap meets a live instrument with a compromised custody history and a payee who had no way to protect her identity. The underlying transaction was an entity disbursement. I am not asking the CFPB to review the originating entity 's internal governance, administrative rights, or entitlement to funds. I am strictly asking the CFPB to review what U.S. Bank did and failed to do after one of its own official checks entered circulation bearing my identity. What Happened Official Check # XXXX was issued in my name on XX/XX/year>, and mailed via regular USPS First-Class Mail without tracking, without mailing confirmation, and without my knowledge or consent. I was not consulted about how the instrument would be sent. I was not informed until it was already in circulation. A {$5000.00} negotiable instrument bearing my legal name and mailing address entered the public mail stream with zero accountability infrastructure and zero input from the person whose identity was on it. It never arrived. On XX/XX/year> On Day 15 following issuance, I contacted U.S. Bank 's Fraud Liaison Unit not to obtain account information, but to provide it. The Fraud Liaison refused to open a case. No check number was requested. No intake occurred. No mechanism existed for a named payee to submit risk information about an active instrument bearing her own identity. I then filed reports with the USPS Postal Inspection Service and local law enforcement. On XX/XX/year> I executed a notarized Affidavit of Non-Receipt and Non-Negotiation and presented it personally at a U.S. Bank branch in XXXX, California. No intake occurred. XX/XX/XXXX XX/XX/year> I contacted multiple U.S. Bank personnel by email. No substantive response was received. On XX/XX/year> I was informed by the originating remitter without documentation that the instrument had been returned to sender, that a stop-payment had been initiated, that the stop-payment had been reversed, and that the same compromised instrument had been re-mailed. I was not asked. I was not notified in advance. I can not help but consider whether earlier bank intervention, had any reporting mechanism existed, might have prevented that second circulation entirely. The bank 's structural blind spot removed the only friction that might have stopped it. When the instrument arrived by Certified Mail on XX/XX/XXXX, I was handed an impossible choice. Accept it and contradict my sworn affidavit, waive all objections to the 29-day custody gap, and absorb every unresolved risk alone. Or refuse it, and watch the instrument re-enter circulation, my PII remain exposed, and control return to the party that created the problem. I refused. There was no option that protected me. On XX/XX/year> I contacted the Fraud Liaison Unit again. Still no meaningful intake occurred. Later that day, I reached branch personnel directly at the issuing location for the first time. I submitted affidavits, police reports, USPIS confirmation, and a complete chronology. U.S. Bank 's Executive Communications unit acknowledged receipt twice, in identical language, and provided no substantive response either time. The Harm I can not prove the instrument was intercepted, copied, or washed during those 29 days. Neither can anyone else. That uncertainty does not resolve in my favor ; it lives on my shoulders indefinitely. I am not the bank 's account holder. I am not the remitter. I am the person whose legal name and address are printed on a {$5000.00} negotiable instrument that floated untracked and unsecured through the public mail stream for nearly a month without my consent and without any mechanism for me to report the risk. I have been a Marcus savings account customer since XXXX. In XX/XX/XXXX, I became aware of a promotion offering a {$1500.00} bonus for depositing {$100000.00} in new funds and maintaining those funds in a Marcus account for 90 days. Because I already had an existing Marcus savings account, I contacted Marcus before moving any money to confirm that existing customers were eligible to participate in the promotion. After more than 90 days had passed, I checked my account and discovered that the promised bonus had not been credited. When I contacted Marcus, I was informed that I was ineligible because I had not completed a separate enrollment process. The representative further stated that many customers had encountered the same issue. I escalated the matter to a supervisor, but again was told only that I had not enrolled and therefore would not receive the bonus. My complaint is not simply that I missed a procedural step. My concern is that the enrollment requirement appears to function as a barrier that predictably disqualifies consumers who otherwise satisfy the substantive requirements of the promotion. Marcus representatives themselves acknowledged that many customers fail to complete this step. If large numbers of consumers are being denied an advertised bonus for the same reason, that raises serious concerns about whether the requirement is being communicated effectively and transparently. As an existing customer, I was not opening a new account. I was responding to a promotional offer that required a deposit of new funds and a 90-day holding period. In that context, the term " enrollment '' was not presented to me as a critical requirement carrying a {$1500.00} consequence. The denial of a {$1500.00} bonus based solely on a missed procedural step is particularly troubling where the consumer has fully satisfied the economic substance of the promotion by depositing and maintaining {$100000.00} in new funds for the required period. What concerns me most is that the enrollment requirement serves no apparent substantive purpose. Marcus already knows when a customer deposits qualifying new funds and maintains those funds for the required period. If enrollment were truly intended to ensure informed participation rather than to create a procedural hurdle, Marcus could easily implement safeguards such as automatic prompts, warning messages before qualifying transfers, follow-up reminders, account notifications, or other mechanisms that would alert customers that an additional action is required. Instead, customers can deposit substantial sums, maintain those balances for months, and only later discover that they have been disqualified from receiving the advertised bonus. The practical effect of the current process is that XXXX receives the benefit of qualifying deposits while retaining the ability to deny the advertised bonus based on a procedural requirement that many consumers apparently overlook. Based on my experience and the number of similar complaints publicly reported by other consumers, this does not appear to be an isolated incident but rather a recurring source of consumer confusion. I have seen consumer complaints about this issue on CFPB, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX and other financial sites and social media. I attempted to resolve this matter directly with XXXX. I submitted a written complaint and sought reconsideration of my eligibility. Rather than addressing the substance of my concerns, Marcus repeatedly relied on the same response : that I had not enrolled. The bank did not address whether the enrollment requirement was adequately disclosed, whether the promotional process is reasonably understandable to existing customers, or whether recurring consumer confusion suggests deficiencies in the design or administration of the promotion. I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed to determine whether Marcus 's promotional practices, disclosures, and complaint-handling procedures are consistent with principles of fair and transparent treatment of consumers. I also request that Marcus reconsider its decision and honor the {$1500.00} promotional bonus based on my deposit of {$100000.00} in new funds and my compliance with the 90-day holding requirement. Thank you for your attention to this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: I, XXXX XXXX, owner of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, submit this complaint against Wells Fargo Bank N.A for its wrongful handling of a XXXX chargeback dispute ( reason code 10.4 - other fraud, card absent environment ) The financial harm to my business resulted from two distinct failures ; Wells Fargo 's failure to follow XXXX XXXX mandated dispute investigation procedures for card-not-present fraud and XXXX XXXX automatic deduction of transaction processing fees and dispute fees, which I was charged despite the dispute being incorrectly decided against me. Wells Fargo 's mishandling of this dispute led to an incorrect chargeback decision that caused direct and material financial harm to my business. MERCHANT ROLE IN THE TRANSACTION XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a registered merchant operating on the XXXX XXXX platform, which uses XXXX as its payment processor. The following describes how transactions are processes in the environment, and why the merchant bears no responsibility for cardholder registration, verification or authorization. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( merchant ) has no involvement in bidder registration and does not handle, enter, or store any card credentials. The merchant does not perform and is not authorized to perform any verification, authentication, or authorization of payments. All cardholder data is transmitted directly and exclusively from the cardholder to XXXX. The merchant is never is possession of this information. Charges are processed and authorized automatically through XXXX 's secure, tokenized payment system entirely without merchant involvement. The merchant 's only visibility into a customer 's account is the name, billing and shipping addresses and last four digits of the card number - information already verified and authenticated by XXXX and the issuing bank prior to authorization. FACTS OF THE TRANSACTION On XX/XX/year> bidder XXXX XXXX registered on the XXXX XXXX platform. He purchased multiple lots of fine jewelry totaling {$3800.00}. Following the auction XXXX XXXX contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX via email and requested that the items be shipped to the shipping and billing address on file with the XXXX XXXX platform. A shipping and insurance fee of {$120.00}. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX fulfilled the order in the full compliance with platform procedures. The goods were delivered to the verified billing and shipping address provided by the buyer. The billing and shipping address were identical. On XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX received notice of a chargeback dispute for the full amounts of {$3800.00} and {$120.00}. All relevant evidence was promptly submitted to XXXX in response to the dispute. WELLS FARGO 'S DISPUTE DECISION ; On XX/XX/year> Wells Fargo issued its dispute decision in favor of the cardholder. The bank 's stated rationale was as follows : ( Our center has certified that this is an unauthorized transaction. The merchant provided no proof that our cardholder authorized the disputed transaction. Neither the name nor the address provided by the merchant matches our cardholder 's profile. The cardholder denies participation in the transaction, engagement with the merchant, or receipt of services. We have met all technical and certification requirements. The account was closed, placed on the exception file, and reported to XXXX as having been used fraudulently. Our cardholder is due full credit ) Wells Fargo categorized the dispute under XXXX Reason Code 10.4 ( other fraud card absent environment ) GROUNDS FOR COMPLAINT a ) The merchant XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX can not provide authorization proof. Wells Fargo 's decision faults the merchant for failing to provide proof that the cardholder authorized the transaction. This requirement is factually and procedurally impossible to satisfy. As described above, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has no role in the authorization process. The merchant never handles card credentials, does not interact with XXXX or Wells Fargo 's authorization system, and is not provided with any authorization codes, CVV results, or AVS response coded. The information merchant submitted- the buyer 's name, billing and shipping address is the information that XXXX presented to Wells Fargo during the authorization request. If that information did not match Wells Fargo 's records, the bank had both the ability and the obligation to decline the transaction at the point of authorization. WELLS FARGO FAILED ITS DUTY AT THE POINT OF AUTHORIZATION Under XXXX Rules and XXXX Product and Service Rules, when an authorization request is submitted, the issuing bank is responsible for verifying cardholder credentials including name, billing address, and card validation codes against its own records. If those credentials do not match the issuer is required to return a decline response, such as Response Code 93 ( transaction can not be completed ) By approving the XXXX tokenized request, Wells Fargo effectively certified that the credentials presented were valid and acceptable. The bank can not now claim that the name and address did not match its records, while simultaneously having approved the transaction. These positions are mutually contradictory. The merchant had no mechanism to perform these checks and no access to the results of any AVS or CVV verification. Chargeback liability can not be assigned to a party who is structurally excluded from the authorization process. ASSIGNEMENT OF CHARGEBACK LIABILITY VIOLATES CARD NETWORK RULES XXXX XXXX own rules prohibit issuers from assigning chargeback liability to merchant under the following circumstances ; Merchants did not process or authorize the transaction. Merchant relied on processor level ( XXXX ) authentication and tokenization. The issuer approved the transaction through its own authorization system. FINANCIAL HARM FROM INCORRECTLY ASSESSED FEES In addition to the chargeback amount itself, XXXX automatically deducted transaction processing fees and dispute fees from my account in connection with these chargebacks. These fees were assessed despite the fact that the dispute was incorrectly decided and the merchant bore no responsibility. RELIEF REQUESTED XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX respectfully requests that the CFPB take the actions ; Direct Wells Fargo to reverse both chargebacks ( {$3800.00} and {$120.00} ), Direct Wells Fargo to reimburse all XXXX dispute fees assessed to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX as a result of this incorrectly decided dispute. I certify that the information in this complaint is true and accurate to the best of my knowledge. All supporting documentation will be submitted to this complaint. XXXX ( XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/year> 2026
